articles.title: Women's Super League: York Valkyrie win 12-0 at Leeds Rhinos to book Grand Final place vs defending champions Wigan Warriors
articles.summary: York Valkyrie are through to the 2026 Women's Super League Grand Final against Wigan Warriors following a superb 12-0 semi-final away victory over Leeds Rhinos.
articles.body:
Tries from Liv Wood, Adaoha Akwiwu, in addition to penalty and conversion from Tara Jane Stanley sees York Valkyrie win Women's Super League semi-final at Leeds Rhinos; Watch Grand Final between Wigan and York live on Sky Sports on Sunday September 27 (5.30pm kick-off)

York Valkyrie are through to the 2026 Women's Super League Grand Final against Wigan Warriors following a superb 12-0 semi-final away victory over Leeds Rhinos.

York will now face defending champions Wigan in the Grand Final at the Brick Community Stadium on Sunday September 27 (5.30pm kick-off), live on Sky Sports.

York, who were beaten 38-16 by Leeds on August 8, and 44-0 by Wigan a week later on August 15, have totally turned fortunes around since, defeating Leeds at home, St Helens away and Wigan at home before sealing semi-final success.

The opening 21 minutes proved scoreless at Headingley in a tight contest, before York's Liv Wood twisted, turned and wrestled over to ground the ball for a try in the 22nd minute. Tara Jane Stanley converted for the full haul.

As the first half drew to a close and with Leeds camped on the York try-line on the verge of a try, a grubber-kick on the last by Leeds' Ruby Walker proved a poor one and allowed Stanley to gather and run clear.

Instead, York were next to add points as Stanley struck a penalty superbly from distance for a lead of 8-0 three minutes from the end of the half.

Eight minutes into the second half, Stanley accelerated forward and forced her way over for York's second try and clear daylight on the scoreboard - but the Video Ref then proved via replays she lost control in the act of scoring to rule it out.

Buoyed by their reprieve, Leeds came back attacking hard at York, but Valkyrie defended superbly to keep their two-score lead intact.

On the hour mark, Leeds' Georgia Elliston powered her way over under the sticks for a try, but again the score was ruled out by the Video Ref, who ruled obstruction.

York then wrapped up victory through Adaoha Akwiwu's try as she burst through off a Stanley short-ball pass for a 12-0 advantage.

With six minutes remaining, Leeds' Ebony Stead appeared to charge over for a try out wide to give Rhinos brief hope, but for a third time on the night the Video Ref ruled out a score, as replays proved Stead had lost control of the ball while going over.

The contest ended on a sour note for York too, with the news Stanley - their standout performer on the night - had failed a Head Injury Assessment (HIA), ruling her out of the Grand Final.

Pryce: Nobody gave us a chance - we've made it against all odds

York Valkyrie head coach Leon Pryce to Sky Sports:

"This is unbelievable. Nobody gave us a chance.

"Everyone had written us off, and last week they were saying it was going to be another Saints vs Leeds game after Saints won here.

"We read the comments and used that as fuel. I don't think we got the respect we deserved, but they've been unbelievable.

"To come to Leeds in a semi-final against a really good squad and keep them to zero just shows.

"It was going to be about grit, toughness and determination.

"Against all odds we've got there and I couldn't be more proud.

"I've been proud of them all season, but the last four or five weeks we've really turned a corner and we don't want the season to end."

Wigan trio make up shortlist for 2026 Woman of Steel

Wigan Warriors will dominate the 2026 Woman of Steel awards, with three players from the reigning Women's Super League champions shortlisted for the competition's most prestigious individual honour.

Jenna Foubister , Eva Hunter and Megan Williams have all been named on the three-player shortlist ahead of Rugby League Awards Night in Manchester, which will take place on the evening of Tuesday September 29.

Foubister's nomination comes after another influential season at the heart of Wigan's attack in 2026. The 19-year-old half-back contributed a return of nine tries in 18 appearances across all competitions and has continued to establish herself as one of the leading playmakers in the women's game. Foubister also produced a Player of the Match performance in the Women's Challenge Cup Final at Wembley Stadium, creating two tries and providing three line-break assists as the Warriors lifted the trophy for a second time.

Reigning Woman of Steel Hunter has enjoyed another prolific campaign under Denis Betts, crossing for 23 tries in all competitions. The dynamic second-rower has continued to showcase her devastating pace, powerful ball-carrying and defensive intensity throughout the season, while also writing her name into the history books by becoming the first woman to score four tries in a Challenge Cup Final at Wembley Stadium.

Williams' place on the Woman of Steel shortlist follows a remarkable first two seasons with the Cherry & White, having quickly established herself as one of the competition's most consistent forwards. Since joining the club ahead of the 2025 campaign from St Helens, the England Knights international has become a key figure in Betts' side. The loose forward has scored four tries since the competition split into the Super Four phase, helping Wigan maintain their push for another historic season.

Watch the Women's Super League Grand Final between Wigan Warriors and York Valkyrie live on Sky Sports on Sunday September 27, with kick-off at 5.30pm.

articles.summary: La verdadera razón por la que Luis Díaz no jugará con la Selección Colombia
articles.body: La reciente convocatoria de la Selección Colombia generó sorpresa tras confirmarse la ausencia de Luis Díaz, uno de los principales referentes atacantes del país. Ante las especulaciones sobre su descarte del equipo nacional, el director técnico Néstor Lorenzo reveló en rueda de prensa los detalles de la conversación previa que sostuvo con el futbolista. Lejos de tratarse de una decisión técnica vinculada a su rendimiento o a una salida definitiva del proceso de la Tricolor, Lorenzo explicó que la no inclusión del atacante responde a una decisión consensuada para priorizar su recuperación física. "Hablé con él y le dije: 'Te veo cansado, Lucho. No tienes el sprint que es tuyo, ¿qué te pasa?', y bueno, consensuamos que descanse esta fecha porque tiene más de 60 partidos", señaló el estratega argentino. El atacante ha enfrentado una alta exigencia en el inicio de la temporada con el Bayern Múnich, donde acumula una importante carga de minutos y partidos consecutivos. Aunque ha recibido observaciones por su falta de gol en compromisos recientes, su entrenador en el club alemán, Vincent Kompany, ha respaldado públicamente al colombiano destacando su rendimiento en los entrenamientos. La pausa de Díaz coincide con un proceso de ajuste en la plantilla de la Selección Colombia. Para esta fecha, el cuerpo técnico aprovechó la oportunidad de citar e integrar nuevos talentos al equipo, entre los que destacan nombres como Camilo Durán, Juan Manuel Rengifo, Daniel Arcila, Matías Orozco y Viveros, entre otros. Asimismo, el estratega confirmó cambios en su cuerpo de asistentes con la incorporación de José Bazán, Christian Ozorno y Ariel Cerulli, marcando una etapa de recambio en la estructura del combinado nacional.

articles.title: Cubs Issue Emotional Statement on Beloved Hall of Famer Ryne Sandberg
articles.summary: The Cubs issued an emotional statement honoring Hall of Famer Ryne Sandberg on what would have been the Chicago legend’s 67th birthday. The post Cubs Issue E...
articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs are in the midst of an intense race for the postseason, with only a one-game lead over the San Diego Padres in the third and final National League wild-card spot.

But before they opened a crucial three-game series in Cincinnati against the Reds Friday, the Cubs took a moment to issue an emotional statement on one of the most beloved, and best, players ever to call Wrigley Field home.

The Cubs honored Ryne Sandberg on what would have been his 67th birthday Friday, posting a tribute nearly 14 months after the Hall of Fame second baseman's death.

"Happy birthday, Ryno. We miss you every day," the team wrote in a social media post Friday.

Sandberg died July 28, 2025, at 65 following a lengthy fight with prostate cancer, according to the Society for American Baseball Research . He had announced the diagnosis in January 2024, appeared to beat the disease by August of that year, then revealed four months later that the cancer had returned and spread.

Ryne Sandberg's Rise to Chicago Cubs Stardom

Born Ryne Dee Sandberg on Sept. 18, 1959 , in Spokane, Washington, he was named after former Yankees pitcher Ryne Duren and earned football honors as a Parade magazine All-American quarterback, and also starred in basketball before choosing baseball. But he was seen as a long-shot prospect. The Philadelphia Phillies drafted him out of Spokane's North Central High School in the 20th round in 1978. They called him up in September 1981.

The Phillies, still not seeing a future in Sandberg, traded the then-22-year-old utility infielder, along with Larry Bowa, to the Cubs that offseason for Iván DeJesús , in a deal that reshaped both franchises' fortunes.

Moved to second base in 1983, Sandberg won a Gold Glove in his first full season there and broke out in 1984, hitting two game-tying home runs off Cardinals closer Bruce Sutter in a nationally televised game that became known as the "Sandberg Game."

That win helped Chicago capture its first postseason berth since 1945, and he closed the year with the NL MVP award, according to the Chicago Sun-Times .

He went on to make 10 straight All-Star teams, collect nine Gold Gloves and seven Silver Sluggers, and led the National League with 40 home runs in 1990, the first second baseman since Rogers Hornsby in 1925 to top the league in homers, according to the National Baseball Hall of Fame .

Over 16 seasons, mostly with the Cubs, he finished with a .285 average, 2,386 hits, 282 home runs and 1,061 RBI, numbers that sent him to Cooperstown in 2005.

Why Chicago Cubs Fans Still Cherish Ryne Sandberg

The Cubs retired Sandberg's No. 23 later that year, making him the fourth player in franchise history to receive that honor. He returned to the organization afterward as an ambassador, greeting fans and representing the club at events, and in June 2024 the team unveiled a statue of him outside Wrigley Field .

At that ceremony, Sandberg joked that he had more gloves than bats stashed in his locker when he first arrived in Chicago.

"Ryne Sandberg was a hero to a generation of Chicago Cubs fans," Cubs chairman Tom Ricketts said following his death, a tribute that still resonates on his birthday, as quoted by the Chicago Sun-Times .

Sandberg's quiet intensity, defensive excellence and refusal to chase the spotlight made him a rare crossover star for a franchise that endured decades without a championship. Fans who grew up watching him anchor second base during the day-game era at Wrigley Field still gather at his statue and mark anniversaries of the Sandberg Game.

Friday's tribute keeps that connection alive, reminding a fan base still chasing October baseball that Sandberg remains central to what it means to wear a Cubs uniform.

articles.title: The 10 Highest-Paid Sports Media Personalities Right Now
articles.summary: Throughout the world of sports entertainment, the most prominent names in broadcasting have become very expensive personalities.
articles.body:
Throughout the world of sports entertainment, the most prominent names in broadcasting have become very expensive personalities.

In recent years, for example, Stephen A. Smith signed a five-year, $105 million extension at ESPN. That pricey agreement pushed Smith to the throne of annual earnings, surpassing the massive deal Fox analyst Tom Brady signed.

And it appears fellow ESPN personality Pat McAfee may soon surge past Smith .

Although exact numbers are not always available, these rankings are based on the most recent reporting from reputable sources.

One unforgettable voice in broadcasting, Al Michaels has been a critical piece of the sports media landscape for 50 years.

Michaels' travels have guided him from CBS and NBC to ABC and now Amazon, where he calls Thursday Night Football games. Marchand , today of The Athletic, reported Michaels made $15 million annually on his initial Amazon deal, which is continuing on a year-to-year basis.

The "Big Diesel" is making big money as an NBA analyst.

Upon retiring from the Association in 2011, Shaquille O'Neal joined TNT Sports. He recently signed a "long-term" extension worth $15 million annually, per Michael McCarthy and Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports.

Kirk Herbstreit rose to prominence in his analyst role on ESPN's College GameDay , and he's parlayed that success into an NFL job.

In addition to his GameDay role, he provides color on ABC's prime-time Saturday college game and Thursday's NFL game. Herbstreit earns $6 million annually from ESPN/ABC and an eight-figure salary from Amazon, per Marchand.

For nearly three decades, Joe Buck spearheaded Fox's coverage for the NFL and MLB. He left for ESPN in 2022, now serving as the play-by-play voice on Monday Night Football . Buck also called an Opening Day MLB game in 2025.

According to Andrew Marchand , then of the New York Post , Buck signed a five-year, $75 million agreement to join ESPN. He's since extended with the company for six years at roughly $108 million , per Marchand.

After his 14-year career with the Dallas Cowboys ended in 2016, Tony Romo soared onto the airwaves for CBS.

Marchand reported in 2020 that Romo, who initially signed a three-year contract, inked a 10-year, $180 million extension. During the NFL season, he's the color analyst for CBS' featured game alongside Jim Nantz, although his status moving forward is unclear after his DUI arrest in July 2026.

Troy Aikman shook up the NFL broadcasting space in 2022, leaving Fox after two decades to serve as ESPN's analyst on Monday Night Football .

According to Marchand , the five-year contract falls in the "$90 million-and-change range" for Aikman.

Following a 16-year NBA career, Charles Barkley went directly to TV. He's been a beloved figure on the Inside the NBA studio show since 2000.

Barkley landed a 10-year extension from TNT (Warner Bros. Discovery Sports) in 2022. Later, he told Marchand the contract is worth $210 million.

The most interesting man in sports entertainment these days, Pat McAfee has been a rapidly rising star in the industry.

McAfee, who punted for the Indianapolis Colts from 2009-16, agreed to a five-year, $85 million contract with ESPN in 2022, per Marchand . He hosts The Pat McAfee Show , serves as an analyst for College GameDay and in 2026 added a spot on Monday Night Countdown , as well.

The growing responsibilities, according to Marchand , have pushed his salary to $30 million with negotiations for an extension worth $60-plus million.

Even before he hung up the cleats, Tom Brady had a broadcasting move locked in. He agreed to a 10-year, $375 million deal with Fox in 2022, per Marchand .

Brady retired after that season, spent a year outside of football and entered the Fox booth in 2024. Alongside play-by-play man Kevin Burkhardt, Brady is the lead analyst on Fox's weekly top NFL game.

Stephen A. Smith's reputation as the loudest voice in sports media has resulted in several major sources of income.

Along with his recent five-year, $105 million deal at ESPN, Smith has a three-year contract for $36 million at SiriusXM Radio. According to Marchand , revenue from his YouTube channel and podcast push Smith into the $40 million range annually.

articles.title: ¿Quién heredará la emblemática '10' de James Rodríguez en la nueva Selección Colombia?
articles.standfirst: Sin James Rodríguez: Néstor Lorenzo suelta una pista sobre quién heredará la '10' de Colombia
articles.summary: Sin James Rodríguez: Néstor Lorenzo suelta una pista sobre quién heredará la '10' de Colombia
articles.body: La incertidumbre sobre el futuro de la camiseta número 10 en la Selección Colombia ha comenzado a despejarse. Tras confirmarse la ausencia de James Rodríguez en las convocatorias recientes, la gran interrogante entre la afición y los medios era si el mítico dorsal sería guardado o si un nuevo jugador asumiría la responsabilidad de portarlo. En la rueda de prensa donde presentó la lista de convocados para los próximos partidos amistosos internacionales, el director técnico Néstor Lorenzo abordó el tema entre bromas y certezas, dejando pistas claras sobre lo que sucederá con la icónica prenda. Con su habitual estilo cercano, el estratega argentino comenzó bromeando sobre la búsqueda de un referente: “Estuve pensando en llamar al 'Pibe' Valderrama (risas). Seguramente la camiseta 10 se va a usar, y es una camiseta honorable para la Selección Colombia, pero hay jugadores que la van a usar y van a jugar bien. Vemos que hay madera y ya va a aparecer el '10' que enamore nuevamente a la hinchada”, declaró Lorenzo. De esta forma, el seleccionador descartó que el dorsal vaya a ser retirado temporalmente. Para la 'Tricolor', el número 10 es un símbolo de identidad y talento que continuará en circulación durante los partidos de preparación. Sin Juan Fernando Quintero en el radar de esta convocatoria —tras anunciar que daba un paso al costado en el equipo nacional—, la responsabilidad recaerá en las nuevas figuras del mediocampo cafetero: El heredero oficial de la camiseta '10' se dará a conocer una vez la plantilla se reúna de forma completa en la concentración para la asignación de números previa a los juegos frente a México, Paraguay y Perú.

articles.title: Leeds United Outcast On Why He Wanted To Leave The Club: Were The Whites Right To Let Him Leave?
articles.summary: Wilfried Gnonto has explained why he pushed to leave Leeds United for Fiorentina during the summer transfer window. The 22-year-old Italian winger told La Na...
articles.body:
Wilfried Gnonto has explained why he pushed to leave Leeds United for Fiorentina during the summer transfer window. The 22-year-old Italian winger told La Nazione, as relayed by Sport Witness , that he did everything possible to complete the move after hearing about the Serie A club's interest. He described his final season in England as frustrating and said returning to Italy could help his national team prospects.

Gnonto made 29 appearances across all competitions during the 2025/26 campaign, although Leeds United restricted him to 867 minutes. He scored one goal and provided four assists. Meanwhile, the winger's wider Leeds record stands at 23 goals and 17 assists in 147 matches.

"I took it easy. As soon as I heard about Fiorentina, I did everything I could to be here," he said.

"I needed something different; last season wasn't the best for me. Being in Italy makes a bit of a difference in terms of the national team. Coming back was the right choice for me; it was easy to adapt; my teammates are all very open and welcomed me really well."

"There was no rush to return, but if Fiorentina calls you, it's different. As an Italian, I know what this team represents in Italy and for the city of Florence. It's an honour to be here. I grew in many ways abroad, first and foremost as a person, and I even got my driving license in a foreign country. I hope to bring these experiences here to Italy."

Leeds confirmed the season-long loan on September 1, with an option for Fiorentina to buy him permanently.

Did Leeds United make the right decision on Wilfried Gnonto?

CHICAGO, ILLINOIS – AUGUST 02: Dominic Calvert-Lewin #9 of Leeds United celebrates his second goal with Wilfried Gnonto #29 against Liverpool FC during the second half at Soldier Field on August 02, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Daniel Bartel/Getty Images)

Leeds United had a reasonable footballing case for allowing Gnonto to leave, although his departure was risky. The Italian winger struggled for regular minutes under Daniel Farke, and his comments suggest that he wanted a fresh start rather than another season on the fringes.

Farke's preference for defensive discipline and pressing placed a premium on consistent work without the ball. Gnonto's limited playing time reflected that selection reality, yet his ability to carry the ball, beat defenders and create chances gave Leeds United a useful attacking option. Losing that profile leaves the squad with less variety.

The club's decision looks more practical because Leeds secured Jean-Matteo Bahoya from Eintracht Frankfurt before completing Gnonto's exit. That move helped address the immediate need for another wide attacker. Still, replacing a player's technical qualities involves more than filling a position on the team sheet.

Noah Okafor 's arrival gives Leeds another option on the left, while Gnonto's loan allows him to pursue regular football in Italy. Fiorentina have already seen an early return, with the winger scoring during a 3–0 Coppa Italia victory over Pisa .

articles.title: Sensational right-back confirms he's ready to join Liverpool
articles.summary: An exciting right-back has just confirmed with his brilliant performance that he's ready to join Liverpool. Since Trent Alexander-Arnold left the club the Re...
articles.body:
An exciting right-back has just confirmed with his brilliant performance that he's ready to join Liverpool .

Since Trent Alexander-Arnold left the club the Reds have had a real issue with the right side of their defensive department.

Alexander-Arnold was so good for so many decades, Liverpool never really had to worry about the position. If anything, his brilliance only forced out very talented players - like Neco Williams for example - who could not get enough game time.

After Trent left, his departure has left a gaping void in the squad.

Especially because his natural successor Conor Bradley is far too injury prone. Even before suffering his devastating injury against Arsenal last season, Bradley on average has missed around 20 games a season in all competitions.

Liverpool's temporary solution to the right-back problem

Naturally, Liverpool did try to replace Alexander-Arnold. They signed Jeremie Frimpong . But it has become apparent very quickly that he isn't really a natural right-back.

Arne Slot and now Andoni Iraola have both opted to play Frimpong further forward.

The former's solution was to play Dominik Szoboszlai in the right-back role instead. It's a role the Hungarian did well. However, long-term Szoboszlai clearly sees himself as a midfielder.

So, in order to appease him Iraola has come up with a different temporary solution. He's decided to play Ronald Araujo there, who has impressed.

But long-term Liverpool will need a new right-back, and it looks like the solution is emerging as we speak.

Daniel Banjaqui's performance confirms he's ready to join Liverpool

The Portuguese teenager has been linked with the Reds for some time. Anfield Watch understands Pedro Marques is a big admirer of Banjaqui in particular.

The 18-year-old has been described as a right-sided Nuno Mendes , who was another player Liverpool desperately tried to sign to no avail.

With Banjaqui they cannot do the same thing.

The youngster is a phenomenal talent and probably the best right-back prospect around at the moment.

He proved that with a sensational performance on his European debut for Benfica earlier this week. Starting against AC Milan at the San Siro, Banjaqui won the most tackles (7) on the pitch and the most duels (10) all while completing 2/3 dribble attempts and making six passes into the opposition's final third.

Those numbers alone prove just how incredible of a player he is. He can do it all. And a performance like that at the San Siro confirms he's ready to step-up and join Liverpool.

articles.title: Fernando Mendoza made unique decision in first Raiders game of  season
articles.summary: Fernando Mendoza wasn’t on the field for the Raiders’ season-opening win over the Dolphins. The rookie was on the sidelines and chose to wear his helmet for...
articles.body:
Fernando Mendoza wasn't on the field for the Raiders' season-opening win over the Dolphins.

The rookie was on the sidelines and chose to wear his helmet for the entire game. Why?

Rather than wear a headset or earpiece and wear a baseball cap, Mendoza donned the helmet to hear the play call. The backup quarterback said he was never offered a headset or was aware that was an option, but he appreciated the helmet because it made the simulation seem realistic.

"Wearing the helmet is pretty crucial because that's where the play calls come in through, and that's the microphone you hear from the speaker," Mendoza said to Sam Warren of The Athletic. "When I wear the helmet, I can [experience] what I would actually see on the field."

The Raiders drafted Mendoza with the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. While the Indiana product is the face of the future for the franchise, the team has been adamant about slow-playing the rookie's debut.

As long as starting quarterback Kirk Cousins plays well, the Raiders will likely keep Mendoza on the sidelines to continue his development process. The 38-year-old's performance in Week 1 was sufficient, but his limitations were evident against Miami .

Cousins completed 1 of 7 passes on throws traveling 10 or more yards downfield. If the Raiders' offense becomes too predictable because of a poor downfield passing game, then the team may be inclined to turn to Mendoza.

Nevertheless, the rookie remains a backup and that will likely pay off in the long run as Mendoza continues to grow and learn by observing rather than hitting the ground running.

If pressed, Tom would probably shine light on a few bright spots from the 2026 season, if you give him the chance, most notably the emergence of multiple young players and top prospects who should play a major role in the Minnesota Twins' future.

Realistically Joe Ryan and Byron Buxton aren't the future for Minnesota anymore. While both Joe Ryan and Byron Buxton are under contract next season, Buck's health puts his future at risk no matter how badly he wants to stay.

MN Twins' Likely 2027 Rookie of the Year Candidates

Unless something major changes during CBA negotiations this offseason, the Twins will be trading Joe Ryan before he leaves in free agency for what's expected to be a huge payday. In reality, the Twins' future rests on this next wave of young talent.

And given the upside these kids — mostly Kaelen Culpepper , Walker Jenkins , and Emmanuel Rodriguez — have, there's legitimate reason to be optimistic. In fact, all three of the above prospects will maintain their rookie eligibility heading into the offseason, meaning the MN Twins will have three legitimate Rookie of the Year candidates in 2027.

Notable with Kaelen Culpepper landing on the IL. He has just 109 at bats, and has spent less than 45 days on the active roster (IL does not count). He will retain rookie status for 2027 along with Walker Jenkins and Emmanuel Rodriguez. — Ted (@tlschwerz) September 18, 2026

Notable with Kaelen Culpepper landing on the IL. He has just 109 at bats, and has spent less than 45 days on the active roster (IL does not count). He will retain rookie status for 2027 along with Walker Jenkins and Emmanuel Rodriguez.

Promoted in early August , Kaelen Culpepper had plenty of runway to exhaust his rookie status in 2026, had he stayed healthy all season, which has been a trend not just for the prospects in this article, but for most Twins top prospects over the past couple decades.

Most recently, Culpepper was placed on injured reserve with a bad hamstring. Even if he comes back immediately when eligible, the Twins will have just two games remaining on the regular season schedule. With just 31 games played and 109 at bats under his belt, Culpepper still be well short of the 130 at bats needed to exhaust rookie eligibility.

Let's talk about MLB PPI draft picks for a minute…

If any of the aforementioned young Twins were to win Rookie of the Year, it could mean more than just another trophy on the organization's mantle. It could mean an draft pick compensation, via the MLB's Prospect Promotion Incentive (PPI) .

Instituted as a way to incentivize earlier call-ups and more playing time for young talented players who are good enough to make an impact at the big league level, PPI picks come immediately after the first round of the MLB Draft, meaning the opportunity to steal a big time talent the team otherwise wouldn't have access to, unless at the top of the draft.

There are multiple ways to earn one, but a player has to break camp with the Major League club or be called up within two weeks of Opening Day, in order to be eligible. Barring injury, all three of Jenkins, Culpepper and Rodriguez should be on the Minnesota Twins' 26-man roster out of camp next spring.

Players with little or no MLB service time need to break camp with the team or be called up within two weeks of Opening Day. Then they must spend all or most of the year in the big leagues. Then they must either win their league's Rookie of the Year award or place in the top three for MVP or Cy Young. Players who made an Opening Day roster and accrued the service time but didn't factor in any awards that year retain PPI eligibility. Although Culpepper, Jenkins, and Rodriguez each played at the big league level this season, rookie status means they will still be included in pre-season prospect rankings. Players aren't taken out of consideration until they graduate from their rookie status. Culpepper being among that group will help the MN Twins to fare better as those lists roll out.

With that being said, while the Twins would love to see their next wave of youth prove themselves as foundational pieces going forward, all three have areas of their game that need major work this offseason, if they are going to take the next step, especially offensively.

Jenkins has struggled the most amongst the Minnesota rookie trio, so far, currently batting .143 with a .556 OPS. He and the Twins hope he broke Thursday night when he produced three hits for the first time in his MLB career, included a game-tying homer in the 9th inning.

articles.title: Late double helps Man City overcome Liverpool
articles.summary: Manchester City made it three wins from three in the Women’s Super League with two stoppage-time goals securing a 4-2 victory over Liverpool.
articles.body:
Defending Women's Super League champions Manchester City maintained their 100% start to the season as they came from behind to claim a thrilling win against Liverpool.

Two late goals settled the outcome as Reds defender Grace Fisk put through her own net in the 90th minute, before Lauren Hemp raced clear in added time to calmly finish for her second strike on Friday night.

It looked set to be a long night for Liverpool when Hemp ran on to Carlotta Wamser's pass inside from the left and finished past former City keeper Khiara Keating with 13 minutes on the clock.

But the visitors quickly responded through Alice Bergstrom and Vivien Endemann , who took advantage of defensive lapses in the City backline to score.

Liverpool's pressing had already created two opportunities when City gave the ball away in the 19th minute, Bergstrom was played in and she coolly slotted past Ayaka Yamashita .

Ten minutes later City failed to clear a cross from the right and Germany striker Endemann pounced on the loose ball, despite Yamashita getting a hand to her shot.

Khadija Shaw was unlucky to hit the post from a tight angle as the hosts responded well, but she drew City level in first-half injury time through a piece of good fortune.

Hemp's low strike from the left trickled onto the goalline from Keating's parry, and Shaw reacted quickly to bundle the ball home.

The visitors - chasing a first away WSL win against City - started the second half brightly with Endemann creating problems down the left flank and a rogue cross hitting the outside of the post.

But City hit back and would have gone in front from a flowing team move had Keating not tipped over Shaw's close-range effort.

Liverpool were then let off the hook when Jade Rose blazed over after a deep cross bounced off the crossbar, but buckled in a dramatic finale as Fisk converted a Grace Clinton cross past her own keeper before the impressive Hemp confirmed a third successive league win for the hosts.

Man City analysis - Hemp sparkles but defensive concerns remain

This was the first time City have been seriously challenged and they got through it - just.

While they displayed their usual relentless approach when attacking, they looked extremely vulnerable without the ball.

In the first half Laura Blindkilde Brown and Yui Hasegawa were overrun in midfield by the physicality and tenacity of Fuka Nagano and Natalia Ramos, the latter leading Liverpool's press.

City's failure to clear in the build-up to Liverpool's second goal highlighted just how much they miss injured centre-back Rebecca Knaak.

However, the mentality of Andree Jeglertz's squad was impressive as fighting back against a very good Liverpool side was no mean feat.

Another major positive was the continued fine form of Hemp, who was unplayable at times with the ball at her feet and caused Reds right-back Sam Kerr all kinds of problems.

Liverpool analysis - Reds impress but changes come too late

That third-placed Liverpool's vast improvement from this time last year has already become a major theme of the new season was testament to the work of boss Gareth Taylor and his players.

They won the midfield battle hands down in the first half, and forced City into mistakes with their pressing as they did against Charlton and Tottenham .

Endemann in particular was excellent on the left wing, while Spaniard Ramos looks to be a superb midfield signing.

However, despite putting in a great performance, Liverpool were hanging on after City's introduction of Sam Coffey , Aoba Fujino and Kerstin Casparij gave them fresh impetus as well as added quality.

Taylor probably left it too late to bring on fresh legs for his team, and ultimately they could not hang on to suffer a first loss of the campaign.

articles.title: ‘They Got After Us’: Aidan Hutchinson Reveals Why Lions Fell Behind Against Bills
articles.summary: Aidan Hutchinson has spoken after the Detroit Lions put up a less-than-impressive performance against the Buffalo Bills in their 2026 Week 2 game in the NFL....
articles.body:
Aidan Hutchinson has spoken after the Detroit Lions put up a less-than-impressive performance against the Buffalo Bills in their 2026 Week 2 game in the NFL. The Lions lost 41-31 to the Bills, a defeat that Hutchinson described as unavoidable.

Hutchinson decried his overall teammates' performance while calling out a few situations from the game. However, he ends his comments on a rather hopeful and positive note as the team looks towards the rest of the season.

What Aidan Hutchinson Said After Bills Game

Hutchison reportedly exposed Josh Allen to create problems outside the pocket. He also bothered him most about Thursday night, which was how much trouble the Detroit Lions had stopping Buffalo's more conventional running game. Sports analyst Brad Galli reported Hutchinson's comments on the game in a recent X post.

"They got after us, for sure. That was not good enough… I know there will be changes. We're not gonna keep banging our heads against the wall."

The Bills rushed for 203 yards on 36 carries, averaging 5.6 yards per attempt. James Cook III contributed 135 yards and a touchdown, while Allen added 69 yards and two rushing scores.

Many expressed concerns about Cook taking on a larger workload agains t the Lions. He finished with 21 carries and averaged 6.4 yards per attempt. Those numbers can help to understand Hutchinson's post-game concerns.

The Lions should always pay special attention to Allen's ability to extend plays. However, Cook's output meant Buffalo was also winning with its regular rushing attack. The Bills eventually finished with 446 total yards and six touchdowns.

In the Lions' opener, they held the New Orleans Saints to 91 rushing yards in their opener. According to his post-game comments, Hutchinson couldn't identify any practical changes between the Lions' sides of either game.

Hutchinson finished with three tackles , a sack, and two quarterback hits. He also highlighted the team's inability to cave Allen in, especially during a first-half play on which the quarterback escaped. Yet the athlete was careful not to assign blame before reviewing the defensive film. Despite identifying the Bills' playing concepts, he insisted that he was most concerned about his future personal contributions in improving the team's game. Jack Campbell spoke in similar terms, taking personal responsibility during an emotional postgame interview.

The Lions scored 21 points after halftime, but their defense could not provide enough opportunities to complete a comeback. Game recaps showed the Bills repeatedly converting short third downs as Detroit tried to close the gap. Meanwhile, Hutchinson confirmed that the team had the willingness to fight but failed to execute that intention. The 26-year-old claimed the side was decent in the first half. Yet he asserted that the team failed to follow up on its halftime resolve to recover in the second half.

Detroit left Buffalo at 1–1 with plenty of time in the season to correct its problems. For Hutchinson, the franchise must begin by making it difficult for opponents to run plays routinely, even when the quarterback poses an extraordinary challenge.

METAIRIE, La. ( WGNO ) - In the latest episode of What's GoiNg On in Sports? WGNO's Jared Paul Joseph and Meagan Glover preview LSU's primetime showdown against Ole Miss and discuss the New Orleans Saints heading into week two.

The Magnolia Bowl will be a top-10 showdown for the first time in 64 years, last occurring in 1962, but the biggest headline will be Lane Kiffin's returning to Oxford less than a year since heading to Baton Rouge.

"I know obviously a lot is going to be made about me, but this is about the players being prepared really well and playing really well. I told the players {Monday} you don't have anything to worry about, as far as attention on you all week, and there's just going to be so much attention, hatred, everything on me," Kiffin said regarding Saturday's matchup.

The biggest question mark though has been quarterback Sam Leavitt's health status.

LSU listed Leavitt as doubtful for its initial injury report, but local reports said the Arizona State transfer missed Wednesday's session due to back tightness.

The Tigers upgraded Leavitt to questionable on Thursday's report.

However, during an interview with the LHSAA Network, Kiffin still remained vague, regarding the quarterback's status for Saturday.

"We'll see. It's still early. We're still not there yet so we're still looking at everything and, hopefully, everything will be good," Kiffin explained.

No. 7 LSU and No. 8 Ole Miss kickoff their week three showdown Saturday night at 6:30 p.m. on WGNO.

Meanwhile, the New Orleans Saints offense will need to get off to a faster start in week two, after going down 21-0 in the season-opening loss at the Detroit Lions .

Quarterback Tyler Shough recorded a career-high 410 passing yards and three touchdowns, but the former second round pick also turned the ball over three times, including the first play from scrimmage in the third quarter.

"There was a lot to clean up, just as a whole offensive unit and especially myself. I wish I would have just kind of gone through my operation and had cleaner feet earlier on. My feet were too quick, and I was trying to be too perfect," Shough explained.

The Black and Gold do have a key player making his season-debut in week two though: Running back Alvin Kamara.

The 10-year veteran missed a season opener for the first time in his career, while recovering from a knee injury the ball carrier suffered in a joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys during training camp, but Kamara is ready to go.

"I'm going. If it wasn't right, I wouldn't be in so I feel great, moving well, really no limitations," Kamara said.

The Detroit Red Wings hope to solve two problems with a single remedy during the 2026-27 season.

They believe if they can be harder to play against, to be more belligerent, particularly in the offensive zone, it can not only disrupt and wear down the opposition but may lead to more scoring. The Red Wings took a step toward that objective by trading a third-round pick and a seventh to the Vegas Golden Knights this summer for Keenan Kolesar. He finished seventh in the league with 270 hits last season.

"Now we've got to get some other guys that are on our roster that can provide us that and become heavier and harder to play against," Detroit coach Todd McLellan said. "Then collectively we might score more by doing that."

The Red Wings ranked 22nd in the league in scoring last season and 29th at just over 17 hits per game. More hitting also creates a mental edge, undermines an opponent's puck-moving and forces turnovers. Turnovers brought about by a heavy forecheck can lead to goals.

"If I can do what I can do and bring that role, I think guys can feed off it well," Kolesar said.

Kolesar has averaged 262 hits per season for the past five season. Physical play has always seemed contagious

"I would hope so," Kolesar said. "I think there's a room full of proud guys in here that want to turn things around. Maybe the first step is bringing what I can, and see who wants to follow along. The Red Wings do have some young hitters, like Marco Kasper (who led the team in hits), Moritz Seider , Simon Edvinsson , Emmitt Finnie , plus veteran Ben Chiarot.

Prospects Carter Mazur and particularly Michael Brandsegg-Nygard could both add prickliness to the lineup.

"Nygaard's going to make our team harder, assuming he makes the team, which I think he can," McLellan said. "He's going to make our team play a little harder."

articles.title: Cam Skattebo Knows What Awaits Him Against Aaron Donald: ‘I Gotta Get One Yard’
articles.summary: Cam Skattebo is not backing away from the possibility of lining up across from Aaron Donald. The New York Giants running back knows exactly what could be wai...
articles.body:
Cam Skattebo is not backing away from the possibility of lining up across from Aaron Donald . The New York Giants running back knows exactly what could be waiting for him Monday night, especially in a short-yardage situation. Donald's return gives the Los Angeles Rams another major piece up front, however, Skattebo sounds more excited than concerned about testing himself against one of the greatest defensive players of his generation.

The matchup also comes with a simple challenge for Skattebo. If the Giants need one yard and Donald is standing in the hole, there will be no avoiding him.

As reported by NFL Rumors on September 18, Skattebo was asked about potentially f acing Donald in Week 2. The Giants RB acknowledged the unusual circumstances surrounding Donald's return; however, he made it clear that he expects the Rams star to be ready if he takes the field.

"If it is his first game, he's got to be ready for it, just like we do. I'm excited to play against him…if I have to meet him in the hole on 3rd and 1, so be it. I gotta get one yard."

Donald came out of retirement in late August after playing during the 2023 season. He did not travel with the Rams for its Week 1 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, instead continuing his preparation in Los Angeles . On Thursday, Donald practiced in full, and Rams head coach Sean McVay said he was hopeful the veteran defensive tackle would play against the Giants.

For Skattebo, that long layoff does n ot erase what Donald can still bring. He knows there could be some adjustment for the three-time Defensive Player of the Year, but the Giants are preparing for the challenge.

Skattebo's confidence is backed by how he opened his season. He rushed 18 times for 81 yards a nd a touchdown in the Giants' 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys . His physical running style was obvious throughout the game, and he averaged 3.5 yards after contact per carry.

That could make Monday night's matchup especially interesting. The Giants want to establish the run, while the Rams allowed 174 rushing yards in their Week 1 loss to the 49ers. Los Angeles could get a major boost from Donald, but the Giants still have a reason to keep attacking the ground game.

There is also uncertainty around the rest of the Rams' front. Myles Garrett is unavailable after landing on injured reserve following knee surgery, while Omar Speights and Nate Landman are both dealing with injuries and were listed as questionable in the supplied report.

That leaves Donald's potential return as an even bigger storyline; however, Skattebo is not treating him like an untouchable figure. He repeatedly called Donald one of the best ever while making his own responsibility clear.

articles.title: Dolphins’ Chop Robinson ruled out vs. 49ers with concussion
articles.summary: NAPA, Calif.— Miami Dolphins edge defender Chop Robinson was ruled out for Sunday’s game against the San Francisco 49ers due to his concussion. Dolphins coac...
articles.body:
NAPA, Calif.— Miami Dolphins edge defender Chop Robinson was ruled out for Sunday's game against the San Francisco 49ers due to his concussion.

Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said ahead of the team's practice on Friday in Napa that Robinson will not play in Sunday's 4:25 p.m. kickoff at Levi's Stadium.

Hafley said Robinson suffered the concussion during Wednesday's practice. With a short turnaround to navigate the NFL's five-step concussion protocol, Robinson will now look to return the following week when the Dolphins host the Kansas City Chiefs on Sept. 27.

"Chop did sustain a concussion during practice," Hafley said before Friday drills. "He is in the protocol. He will not play this week. He is doing well. And I will leave it at that for Chop questions."

His concussion diagnosis was initially revealed when the Dolphins released their first injury report for the week on Wednesday evening, later than usual as the team practiced on the West Coast between games at Las Vegas and San Francisco .

Robinson, the third-year edge rusher who has an important season ahead of him, was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's drills on the injury report after he was seen practicing early in the session during a media viewing period.

On Thursday, Robinson did not practice. He instead was first seen watching teammates during team stretch, then walking around the perimeter of the Napa facility alongside a trainer before returning to the sideline on the field and watching individual position drills.

It's Robinson's third concussion in the last calendar year. Last season, he suffered one in late October that cost him the following week's game, and late in the year, he had another one, leading him to sit out the season finale.

"That's going to hurt," linebacker Jordyn Brooks said Thursday of the possibility of being without Robinson. "Chop is a great young player who I think is going to be great in this league, so it hurts to have him (out), but it's got to be the next-man-up mentality.

"It's an opportunity when you're the next man up, so I think everybody's aware of that."

Without Robinson, the Dolphins will likely do a number of things up front. For one, they can continue to use defensive tackle Zeek Biggers lined up more on the edge as a defensive end, as he did plenty last Sunday in Las Vegas when he started opposite Robinson. Josh Uche , Malik Herring , Robert Beal Jr. and Clelin Ferrell , who is on the practice squad but is a candidate for elevation again, should receive an uptick in snaps in Robinson's absence.

"It's all of the above," Hafley said. "We might do some other things to help out, but those guys, I have confidence in. They've been getting better. They all haven't been here for the entire time, but they've done a nice job in practice this week, and it'll be the next man up."

Added defensive coordinator Sean Duggan on Thursday: "Your job as a coach is to prepare everybody."

It's a key season for Robinson, the 2024 first-round pick out of Penn State, but it started inauspiciously even before the concussion.

In last week's season-opening loss to the Raiders , he made just one assisted tackle, didn't apply pressure on Las Vegas quarterback Kirk Cousins and was not particularly strong against the run.

"I thought he was a little hesitant," Hafley said Monday of Robinson's Week 1 play. "I don't think he set edges as violently at times as he did. And then, I thought, as the game went on, he got better. We just need him to pick up and then make sure that it's consistent throughout the game."

After this season, the Dolphins will decide on whether to pick up the fifth-year option on Robinson's rookie deal before he goes into his fourth season.

Also ruled out Friday before the Sunday game was linebacker Ronnie Harrison Jr., who aggravated a pre-existing hamstring injury against the Raiders.

Long snapper Tucker Addington's status is in doubt with a shoulder injury, and if he can't play, the team can elevate Cal Adomitis , who was signed this week to the practice squad.

Hafley said he anticipates rookie tight end Seydou Traore would be able to play against the 49ers through thumb and Achilles ailments, barring setbacks.

articles.title: Arthur B. Hancock III, musician and 3-time Kentucky Derby winner, dies
articles.summary: Hancock won the Kentucky Derby three times, including with 1989 U.S. Horse of the Year Sunday Silence. He also is in the Kentucky Music Hall of Fame.
articles.body:
The Mercedes still sits parked next to the main house at Stone Farm.

It's the one Arthur Boyd Hancock III drove to the 1989 Kentucky Derby when he told a police officer, "I have a horse in the Derby," and the officer responded, "Right, and I'm the governor." After the race, security wouldn't let him in the winner's circle. Hancock not only had a horse in the race, he ended up with the winner when Sunday Silence beat the favored Easy Goer to save the farm.

For nearly four decades, that Mercedes has represented the man who lost a lot of hands but never stopped betting on himself.

Hancock, a musician and songwriter who instead chose the family business and became a thoroughbred breeder and owner, thrice winning the Kentucky Derby, died Friday, Sept. 18, from pancreatic cancer, surrounded by his family on his horse farm in Paris. He was 83.

Born to one of America's preeminent horse racing families, Hancock was known internationally for breeding and raising stakes-winning thoroughbreds, including by that 1989 winner, Sunday Silence, who became arguably the most influential stallion in Japan's thoroughbred history and changed the international breeding industry.

Hancock grew up among the hills of bluegrass in Bourbon County. He received a first-class education in horsemanship from his father and grandfather, at times showing first-class interest in music and, as he tells in his book, drinking.

His was a life of prominence, of top quality and also of juxtapositions, perhaps none more striking than that he both won the Kentucky Derby and was inducted into a music hall of fame. He was inducted into the National Museum of Racing and Hall of Fame as a Pillar of the Turf in 2025, and Kentucky's Music Hall of Fame in 2026.

In 2025, he published a memoir entitled "Dark Horses," in which he wrote, "I'm 100% sure I'd have gone into music if I had been born with nothing."

The day after he published, he was diagnosed with the same disease that quickly took his father. The three-time Kentucky Derby winning breeder and owner spent the past two years quietly battling pancreatic cancer.

He and his wife, Staci, have six children (five daughters and one son) and five grandchildren.

One of the first things in life horseman Hancock had to overcome was his name.

His grandfather, Arthur B. Hancock Sr., founded Claiborne Farm in the early 1900s. The farm is and was the legendary home of many horse racing legends, known for breeding champions and standing the world's leading stallions, including Secretariat.

Arthur's grandfather passed the farm to his son, Arthur "Bull" Hancock Jr., who at one time ran the largest thoroughbred operation in the world, nearly tripling Claiborne Farm's size to about 6,000 acres. Arthur learned how to be a horseman from his father, Bull, who also earned acclaim by breeding to European horses, including Princequillo and the Aga Khan's Nasrullah, two of the world's then-champion sires.

While his father could be in a barn 25 hours a day, Arthur also discovered a passion for music. An accomplished musician, he found a home in bluegrass, writing songs recorded by Willie Nelson and Ray Price, and becoming good friends with Peter Rowan, one of Bill Monroe's Bluegrass Boys.

Music would be a constant in Hancock's life, but his father would often tell him, "You can't do two things and do either one well."

Maybe not at the same time, but Arthur is the only man to be named a Hall of Fame horseman — next to the likes of thoroughbred trainer D. Wayne Lukas and Derby-winning jockey Pat Day — as well as a Hall of Fame musician, next to the likes of Loretta Lynn, Patty Loveless, Dwight Yoakam and Chris Stapleton.

After graduating from Vanderbilt with a bachelor's in history, Hancock left Nashville and its music scene and became an assistant to trainer Eddie Neloy at Belmont Park, working with champion Buckpasser.

Leaving Claiborne for a new legacy at Stone Farm

Bull Hancock died of pancreatic cancer two weeks after he was diagnosed in 1972.

In his memoir, "Dark Horses," Hancock wrote about his exit from Claiborne as a disagreement between two of the executors and legendary pillars of the farm, Ogden Phipps and William Haggin Perry, stating that the two told his younger brother, Seth, then just 23 years old, they were planning to make him president and demote Arthur, while keeping that news from Arthur.

"I thought, if that's how they feel, fine," Hancock wrote in his memoir. "I'm not going to hang around if I'm not wanted. … I was shattered. But I knew I had done the right thing, even though it was the hardest thing I had ever done. I was giving up my heritage and my birthright."

The relationship between the two brothers following their father's death, as well as the decision made by farm management, has long been documented in newspaper accounts, industry publications and, of course, Arthur's memoir.

In May, the family told The Courier Journal there is nothing between the brothers now but respect.

"While it was probably a little messy at times, it worked out how it should have worked out," Seth Hancock said. "He is a terrific horseman. While we didn't work side by side, I learned a lot from what he did because he was as good as there ever was at doing it."

The night Arthur left Claiborne, he went to Halls on the River, a quaint restaurant in Winchester. As he tells it in his memoir, Hancock drunkenly told his best friend, Paul Sullivan, that one day he was going to win the Kentucky Derby and "be bigger than Claiborne."

Sullivan responded, "Waitress, bring this fool another Budweiser."

Hancock left Claiborne management and its four-columned mansion for land six miles down the road and a four-room cottage, purchasing Stone Farm in 1964.

"I was going to be a land baron — spelled b-a-r-r-e-n," Hancock wrote in his memoir. He eventually bought 18 farms of "4,600 acres of prime Bourbon County land," making him "one of Kentucky's largest landowners," he wrote.

When he bragged about it to Stone Farm yearling manager Sam Ransom, Hancock's trusted employee responded, "Well, boss, we may be big in size but Claiborne's big otherwise."

The bet on land would soon place him in dire financial pressures.

A Kentucky Derby 'dream' his father never realized

Hancock did get his shot at the Derby. It first came in 1971, when Tap Shoes ran a disappointing leg.

A little more than a decade later, a grey horse named after a cat that liked to lounge around the barn in the sun entered the 1982 Kentucky Derby at 21-1 odds. Gato Del Sol, sired by a Chilean horse named Cougar, had yet to win a race when the 19 horses went to the post.

Gato started from the next-to-outside position. He came from next-to-last, picking off his counterparts along the backstretch before racing three horses wide in the stretch to win the roses by 2½ lengths.

That moment on May 1, 1982, made Hancock the first member of his family to win America's most celebrated race.

Hancock told BloodHorse, an industry trade publication, in 1982: "I had an out-of-body experience for the only time in my life. It was the damnedest thing to be in the winner's circle of the Kentucky Derby. That was Daddy's dream, and it didn't happen for him. But I thanked him on the TV interview for showing me how to get there."

Hancock continued: "I felt redeemed. I remember sitting in a restaurant in Lexington before Gato won, and some guy at the next table was talking about Claiborne and saying how well Seth was running it. And then he says, 'That other brother is a lost ball in high weeds.' I didn't say anything, but I wanted to. After Gato, people began treating me differently."

Still, Hancock nearly went bankrupt in the 1980s — being that "land barren" and accumulating debt he was unsure how he would pay down. In 1988, when the horse and real estate markets crashed, Hancock owed about $15 million on the farm.

Then came that sickly black foal and the Cinderella story of 1989 in Sunday Silence. A son of Halo, the colt fell ill and nearly died on his first Thanksgiving. Owned by Hancock's friend Tom Tatham, the yearling garnered no interest at the Keeneland sale, so he was brought back to the farm. Hancock tried to sell him again at an auction in California, but again nobody wanted the yearling.

On the trip back from California to Kentucky, the horse van overturned. The accident killed several other horses aboard. Sunday Silence survived. It was a sign to Hancock to keep him. In partnership with trainer Charlie Whittingham, the horse showed promise. Then, he won the 1989 San Felipe Handicap and Santa Anita Derby.

Next came the Run for the Roses. Easy Goer was touted as the superior horse, the best ever bred by Ogden Phipps, who was part of the farm management who made the decision to place Seth at the helm of Claiborne. Based on newspaper reports from the time, Easy Goer was considered the second-coming of Man O' War. He was regally bred, sired by Alydar out of a Buckpasser mare named Relaxing. (Alydar had his own legendary rivalry, finishing second to Triple Crown winner Affirmed in all three races.)

Easy Goer was a favorite to win. But it was Sunday Silence's Derby, and then Preakness. Easy Goer denied Sunday Silence the Triple Crown, winning the Belmont Stakes.

But the fourth and final showdown between the two horses in November 1989, the Breeders' Cup Classic, didn't disappoint. Easy Goer was the betting favorite. As the finish line drew close, Sunday Silence had the lead.

"All of a sudden, there (Easy Goer) was, and my heart was in my throat," Hancock wrote in his memoir. "That great racehorse was rolling like a runaway train, gaining ground with every jump. I dropped down on my knees in the front of the box, praying, 'Please God don't let this big red (expletive) catch us,' and for a minute I thought he might. But he didn't get there in time."

Sunday Silence won by a neck. He was later named Horse of the Year.

In retirement, Sunday Silence drew little hype among American breeders. He never covered a mare in Kentucky and was instead offered for sale to stand in Japan. (He was already part-owned by Zenya Yoshida, who bought into the champion at the end of his three-year-old season.) Sunday Silence was Japan's leading sire for 13 years, helping turn Japan's breeding industry into one that consistently produces Derby contenders and has produced legendary Japanese racing champions. He is argued to be the greatest sire in the history of Japanese breeding.

In Hancock's speech at the Eclipse Awards dinner in February 1990, he talked of believing in Sunday Silence and thanked those who believed in him.

"In closing, I want to thank God for the blessing," he said, "but I feel like Kris Kristofferson must have felt when he wrote that beautiful song, 'Why me, Lord?'"

S tephanie Kuzydym is an enterprise and investigative sports reporter. Reach her at skuzydym@courier-journal.com .

articles.title: Inspired Wales seal stunning win over South Africa
articles.summary: Wales return to winning ways in emphatic fashion with an eight-try victory over South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park.
articles.body:
Tries: Keight, Tuipulotu 2, Lockwood, Davies, K Jones, Neumann, Callender Cons: Bell 5

Tries: Jacobs, Tshiremba, Samboya Cons: Dolf 2

Wales returned to winning ways in emphatic fashion with an eight-try victory over South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park.

The hosts had gone nine Tests without a victory heading into their WXV Global Series opener, with a tight contest predicted against a Springboks side ranked three places above them in the world.

But Sean Lynn's bold selections paid off as Wales attacked with a freedom and intent they have not produced for years.

They were six tries to the good in a dominant first half, with the visitors made to pay for indiscipline.

Tighthead Sisilia Tuipulotu was back to her irrestistible best, scoring in either half, while co-captain Alex Callender returned from injury with a typically impressive player-of-the-match display.

Lynn had told his players to be brave in the build-up, and he was courageous with his team selection after moving scrum-half Keira Bevan to 10.

The gamble paid off as the hosts enjoyed a perfect start under Friday night lights and it was fitting that the recently crowned Welsh Rugby Writers' player of the year Courtney Keight bagged the opening score.

Georgia Evans and Tuipulotu had made the hard yards before the ball was spread wide to Keight on the left wing and she cut inside to go over.

Kelsey Jones' turnover provided the launchpad for the second, with Evans popping a neat ball back inside for Tuipulotu to charge to the line.

South Africa responded with Felicia Jacobs benefiting from a dominant scrum on Wales' five-metre line, but that was to be their only score in a one-sided half.

Former Cardiff City footballer Amy Williams came within metres of scoring after winning the footrace to Lisa Neumann's grubber kick, but Seren Lockwood was first to the breakdown and darted over herself.

It was a double blow for the visitors who had hooker Lindelwa Gwala sent to the sin bin for being offside in the build-up.

Wales took full advantage with Maisie Davies showing her power to score her first international try and secure Wales' bonus point.

The hosts were in dreamland, but had to revert to their usual half-back pairing when Lockwood failed to return from a head injury assessment, with Bevan going back to scrum-half and Lleucu George slotting in at 10.

The enforced changes did little to halt Wales' flow with Freya Bell coming agonisingly close from a five-metre driving lineout, but Jones was there to clean up as she crossed over.

South Africa then went down to 13, with lock Danelle Lochner sent to the sin bin for a high tackle on Kate Williams, a card that would later be upgraded to a 20-minute red.

That paved the way for the pick of Wales' first-half tries. A solid scrum provided the platform for the ball to be worked out wide to Neumann who cruised over from her new full-back position.

It was Wales at their clinical best as they headed down the tunnel 38-5 in front.

As we know in Welsh rugby, things are never that straightforward and a wounded South Africa came out a different team in the second half.

Wales had initially picked up where they left off with Tuipulotu powering through some weak tackling for her second of the night to give Wales a 40-point lead.

But South Africa chipped away, with Maria Tshiremba scoring her third try in just two appearances after latching on to a tricky crossfield kick.

They were soon in again with what was arguably the try of the night. It came from the powerful running of Aphiwe Ngwevu who offloaded to her centre partner Maceala Samboya, who showed a good turn of pace to get to the line.

With Wales' defence creaking, they were in need of a little inspiration and that came from Williams, who not only showed great feet down her wing but incredible strength to keep the ball alive for Callender to score.

Front-row forwards Shanelle Williams and Elan Jones came off the Welsh bench to make their debuts and enjoy something many of their team-mates had not experienced in over a year - a Welsh win.

Wales: Neumann; Singleton, Keight, Bell, A Williams; Bevan, Lockwood; Davies, K Jones, Tuipulotu, B Metcalfe, Evans, K Williams (co-capt), Callender (co-capt), King.

Replacements: S Williams, G Pyrs, E Jones, Crabb, Aiono, A Joyce, George, De Vera.

South Africa: Dolf; Tshiremba, Samboya, Ngwevu, Malinga; Van Rensburg, Felicia Jacobs; Charlie, Gwala, Latsha, Ubisi, Lochner, Solontsi, Catha Jacobs, Welman.

Replacements: Gunter, Khuzwayo, Mdliki, Mokwai, Hele, Noxeke, Cilliers, Mokone.

articles.title: Guardians have same 'fatal flaw' for playoffs as Brewers, but with a lot less hope
articles.summary: While the Guardians and Brewers have the same problem, Cleveland's is worse.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Guardians are fighting the Chicago White Sox for the AL Central division title and a chance at a first-round bye. While they've taken the division lead, it could easily slip back out of their grasp.

When it comes to the postseason, the Guardians have some great defense and pitching to rely on. But their offense is a big question mark. More specifically, it's about their power-hitting abilities.

ESPN's David Schoenfield highlighted the "lack of power" as the Guardians' "fatal flaw" this upcoming postseason, which happens to be the same as the Milwaukee Brewers '. But there's one big difference: Cleveland has a lot less hope to overcome this flaw.

Guardians have less hope to overcome 'fatal' power flaw

" Cleveland Guardians . Fatal flaw: Lack of power (tied for 28th in home runs)," Schoenfield writes. "Cleveland falls into the same boat as the Brewers, except the Guardians don't have Milwaukee's ability to hit for average or overall depth."

The Guardians offense isn't in a good spot, as their 147 homers are tied with the Brewers for the second-worst mark in Major League Baseball, just one homer ahead of the Los Angeles Angels .

Either team could end the regular season with the fewest home runs hit in the big leagues this year. That will, obviously, be a huge issue come the postseason.

The Brewers have likely NL Cy Young winner Jacob Misiorowski alongside a strong bullpen and a few other good starters.

While the Guardians won't have a Cy Young winner in the AL, Parker Messick and Gavin Williams alongside Cade Smith make for a strong pitching staff as well.

The reason why there is less hope in Cleveland compared to Milwaukee is the overall offensive production. Going by OPS, the Brewers rank fourth-best in MLB at a .747 OPS.

The Guardians? They come in at second-to-last, 29th overall, with a lousy .689 OPS. The .236 batting average (24th), 604 RBIs (27th), and .375 slugging percentage (29th) are some of the worst offensive marks in baseball.

Sure, the Guardians might have some good players and low strikeout numbers. But their lack of power and overall disappointing offense are likely to prove to be a "fatal flaw" come the postseason.

articles.title: Five things to expect in USC’s Big Ten opener at Rutgers
articles.summary: The Trojans are set to open up Big Ten play this weekend at Rutgers. What can we expect to see in the matchup?
articles.body:
Big Ten play is officially here for USC! After finishing their nonconference slate 3-0, the Trojans will open up conference play on the road this week at Rutgers .

With Trent Mosley out , the Trojans will need their other receivers to step up. They get that from fellow freshman Kayden Dixon-Wyatt, who goes for over 100 yards.

USC defensive lineman Luke Wafle is from New Jersey. Playing his first college football game in his home state, Wafle records at least five total tackles.

USC should have a physical advantage over Rutgers on the lines of scrimmage. The Trojans use this advantage to rush for 200 or more yards.

Quarterback Jayden Maiava has accounted for at least three total touchdowns in each of USC's first three games. He does so again on Saturday.

articles.title: Red Sox Reveal Shuffled Lineup After Willson Contreras Injury Scare
articles.summary: Some changes made in the first of three in Tampa Bay.
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox will begin a potentially season-defining weekend without their leading home run hitter in the starting lineup. Willson Contreras is out Friday as Boston opens a three-game series against the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field. Contreras was struck on the right hand during Thursday's dramatic 4-3 comeback win over the Texas Rangers .

X-rays came back negative, but Contreras experienced swelling and briefly lost feeling in the hand. Interim manager Chad Tracy said the veteran would be evaluated daily. With Contreras sidelined and left-hander Ian Seymour starting for Tampa Bay , Tracy constructed an unconventional batting order featuring several of Boston's right-handed options.

Roman Anthony will lead off and play left field, but Jarren Duran , Masataka Yoshida and Adley Rutschman are among the notable players not starting. Jahmai Jones will serve as the designated hitter and bat third, one spot ahead of Wilyer Abreu . Trevor Story remains in the fifth spot after supplying the biggest swing of Boston's season Thursday. His three-run home run in the eighth inning erased a 3-1 deficit and helped the Red Sox avoid a sweep in Texas.

The Red Sox announced their lineup on Friday afternoon.

The veteran left-hander enters the opener with a 7-4 record, 3.33 ERA and 130 strikeouts across 137 2/3 innings. Suárez also is coming off one of his strongest performances of the season, holding the Kansas City Royals to one run over seven innings last Saturday.

Seymour presents a difficult matchup despite his 4.27 ERA. The Tampa Bay left-hander has recorded 150 strikeouts in 122 1/3 innings while posting a 9-6 record and 1.14 WHIP. His ability to miss bats helps explain Boston's decision to load the lineup with right-handed hitters.

The Red Sox enter Friday at 83-70 after salvaging the finale in Texas. Their postseason magic number sits at three, meaning every victory could move them closer to securing a playoff berth.

Tampa Bay has already clinched a postseason spot and brings a six-game winning streak into the series. The Rays own the American League's best record at 93-59.

First pitch is scheduled for 7:10 p.m. ET from Tropicana Field.

articles.title: Should you start Bucs WRs this week in fantasy football?
articles.summary: Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin lead the Bucs' fantasy options at wide receiver against the Browns in Week 2.
articles.body:
The Buccaneers ' receiving corps is getting healthier ahead of their Week 2 matchup with the Cleveland Browns , which gives fantasy managers more options but also makes the target distribution a little harder to predict.

Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin remain the two Bucs receivers I'm comfortable starting this week. Ted Hurst III and Jalen McMillan are deeper options, but both carry more risk and will likely need to find the end zone to provide enough fantasy value to justify putting them into a lineup.

Egbuka entered the season with plenty of expectations, and his role in Week 1 gave fantasy managers a reason to keep trusting him. He caught five passes for 63 yards against Cincinnati, finishing as Tampa Bay's leading receiver in the loss.

FantasyPros has Egbuka ranked as the WR19 for Week 2 with a projection of 11.1 fantasy points. That's right around where I have him against Cleveland, and I'm comfortable starting him as a WR2 this week.

The return of McMillan adds another receiver to the offense, but it isn't enough for me to move away from Egbuka after one game. He should continue to have a significant role in Tampa Bay's passing attack, making him one of the easier Bucs receivers to put into your lineup.

Godwin is another receiver I'm starting against Cleveland. He caught all four of his targets for 40 yards in Week 1, giving us our first look at how he will be used in Zac Robinson's offense alongside Egbuka.

FantasyPros isn't quite as high on Godwin this week, ranking him WR30 with a 9.6-point projection. I'm a little more comfortable with him than that ranking suggests, especially in PPR formats where his ability to pick up receptions can give him a safer floor.

McMillan's return could take away some opportunities, but Godwin's established role is enough for me to keep him in the lineup. Egbuka has the higher ranking this week, but both are receivers I would feel comfortable starting against the Browns.

Hurst took advantage of McMillan being out in Week 1, catching all three of his targets for 36 yards in his NFL debut. He also received significant playing time as Tampa Bay leaned heavily on three-receiver sets with McMillan unavailable.

The problem this week is that McMillan appears ready to return. He was a full participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday, which could cut into Hurst's opportunities against Cleveland. FantasyPros has Hurst all the way down at WR78 with a 5.2-point projection.

I wouldn't completely rule him out in a deeper league because he could still have a role, but he's going to be difficult to trust with McMillan back. Hurst feels touchdown-dependent this week, and that's too much risk for me in a standard lineup.

McMillan is the most interesting decision of the group because he's coming back from the knee injury that kept him out of Week 1. The good news is that he's been a full participant in practice on both Wednesday and Thursday, which is a strong step toward getting him back on the field Sunday.

FantasyPros ranks McMillan WR93 with a projection of 4.2 points this week. I think there is more upside here than that ranking might suggest, but I'm still waiting a week before putting him into a fantasy lineup.

We haven't seen McMillan play a regular-season game in this offense yet, and we don't know how heavy his workload will be immediately after his return from injury. He could absolutely have a decent game, especially if he finds the end zone, but that's not enough for me to start him until I see his role.

For Week 2, Egbuka and Godwin are the two Bucs receivers I want in my lineup. Hurst and McMillan are deeper options with touchdown-dependent upside, but I'd especially give McMillan one week back on the field before trusting him in a fantasy lineup.

articles.title: Commanders rule out two key starters for Sunday vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: The Commanders will be without two key starters for Sunday's NFC East battle with the Cowboys.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders made it official on Friday. They will be without starting linebacker Frankie Luvu and starting tight end Chig Okonkwo for Sunday's Week 2 game against the Dallas Cowboys .

"Frankie and Chig weren't able to make it back this week," head coach Dan Quinn said on Friday. "Guys are working hard. We'll see what it looks like for next week. So, I wanted to give you all the info I have before we get rolling."

Luvu strained his groin in the third quarter of Washington's Week 1 game against the Philadelphia Eagles , while Okonkwo suffered a hamstring injury. Neither appears to be a long-term issue.

How will the Commanders compensate for Okonkwo's loss?

"It'll have to come obviously in different spaces and people of how we would deploy them," Quinn said. "I'm pleased with the work that I've seen from him, but at that position, we do have guys with some speed that can still bring things vertically down the field. Specifically, Ben [Sinnott] and [Colson] Yank [Yankoff] into those spots. But it's definitely significant."

Fortunately, the Commanders have solid depth at tight end with Sinnott, Yankoff, and blocking ace John Bates . However, none offer the same type of athleticism as Okonkwo. Yankoff could be the one to watch.

Luvu's loss may be even more significant.

"There's an energy that comes with him," Quinn said of Luvu. "I like him as a blitzer. You've seen us feature him in that way this year as opposed to last year. It was more like we did his first year here. And that's a good role for him. He's aggressive. He's flying. So, he does bring a certain energy to the whole group in general. From a communication standpoint, both Sonny [Styles] and Leo [Chenal], too strong suits for them, in control, in command, but we'll definitely miss Frankie in that space."

Washington could elevate linebacker Ale Kaho to provide extra depth. The Commanders also have Kain Medrano , who plays exclusively on special teams. Top reserve linebacker Jordan Magee was placed on injured reserve earlier this week with a hamstring injury.
