articles.title: Ravens Week 2 injury report: Flowers doubtful, 3 starters questionable
articles.summary: The Ravens could be without several key starters in their Week 2 matchup against the Saints.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens are unlikely to have Zay Flowers on the field in Week 2. The star wide receiver has been listed as doubtful with a hamstring injury on the team's final injury report before Sunday's matchup with the New Orleans Saints .

Flowers, 26, racked up 150 yards on just five catches in the first half of the Ravens' Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts before aggravating the hamstring issue that had been bothering him for a few weeks. He returned to practice on Friday in a limited capacity after two absences, but that may not be enough for him to play on Sunday. The two-time Pro Bowler will likely go through a pre-game warm-up, but his designation betrays. the likely outcome.

Here are the rest of Baltimore's Week 2 injury designations:

The Ravens will have to wait another week before getting Buchanan and Madubuike back on the field. Week 3 in Brazil is no guarantee given the additional travel demands. Neither has ramped up to full participation yet, but Baltimore has been planning these players' returns for months. Perhaps one or both advances quickly enough next week to make the trip, but a Week 4 debut feels like a more reasonable projection.

Head coach Jesse Minter has indicated that Tampa could be dealing with a multi-week absence after hurting his knee. He could even be a candidate for injured reserve based on his non-participation in practice all week. That would leave Baltimore short at outside cornerback with two more weeks until Bilhal Kone is eligible to come off injured reserve.

Hendrickson, Simpson, and Stanley are the major questions heading into the weekend. All three missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday before limited participation on Friday.

Hendrickson dominated Colts left tackle Bernhard Raimann in Week 1, generating eight pressures and looking worth every penny of the $112 million contract he signed in Baltimore this offseason. His absence would likely lead to undrafted rookie Ethan Burke getting his first regular-season snaps on defense after playing on special teams in Week 1.

Simpson's replacement at left guard would be Andrew Vorhees or Emery Jones . The former had the starting job last year but lost it due to poor play; the latter played just 49 snaps last year and struggled in the preseason. The Saints do not have an imposing interior defensive line, but even one weak link can collapse an offensive line.

Two weak links would be a disaster. If Stanley is sidelined by his toe injury, 2025 fifth-round pick Carson Vinson would make his first career NFL start against Chase Young , the former No. 1 overall pick who posted a career-high 10 sacks in just 12 games last year. Throw in Jovaughn Gwyn 's underwhelming pass-blocking performance in his first start last week, and this could be trouble.

Baltimore's run game should still hum with Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry toting the football. But the offensive line will have to handle protection adjustments and their 1-on-1 matchups without the penalties that prevented the Ravens from dropping 50 points last week. Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle could use extra protection to protect Jackson's blind side, so this could be a big week for Vega Ioane and Roger Rosengarten to handle business on the right side.

The Saints' injury report includes five players with designations for Sunday's game:

Wood and Stalbird are both special teams contributors whose absence will impact the Saints more than the Ravens. But Olave and Young are two of New Orleans ' most important players. Both got hurt in practice on Thursday and remained limited on Friday; given their injury histories, they are not locks to play in Week 3. Miller, a second-round rookie, played 25 snaps in his NFL debut but injured his toe on Friday, likely making him a game-time decision as well.

articles.title: Only one Juventus player called up for Roberto Mancini’s first Italy squad
articles.summary: It won’t take long to figure out who the one player called into the Italy squad who plays for Juventus is this time around.
articles.body:
Much in the same fashion as Juventus' starting lineup last weekend against Sassuolo , there won't be much of a Bianconeri flavor when the Italian national team meets for their first meet-up at Coverciano during the upcoming international break.

One Italian in the starting lineup last weekend at the Mapei. And now just one Juventus player called into Roberto Mancini's first Italy squad since coming back to coach the Azzurri this summer.

It just so happens to be the same player, goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario , that has that distinction. Thanks to a combination of injuries and Mancini wanting to shake things up in a big way as he begins his second spell in charge, it means Juventus' only player named to the original squad that includes 33 other names — and an very noticeable number of players who don't currently call Serie A home.

Mancini, without a doubt, is casting quite a wide net to try and find some younger options after everything that has happened since the last time he was manager and now. And that involves calling in some names that were completely off the radar just a few months ago.

With Juventus' captain Manuel Locatelli injured, that takes one potential selection out of the equation. Same goes for Andrea Cambiaso , who could make his return to the matchday squad this weekend against Atalanta . Federico Gatti , a player who just started his first game of the season against NEC in the Europa League on Thursday night, probably wasn't even in consideration because of a lack of playing time.

That leaves Vicario, who has previously served as Gianluigi Donnarumma 's backup for a good portion of the last few years no matter who the Italy manager actually is.

And it also means that clubs like Bologna and Cagliari have more players called into the squad than Juventus. It means Juventus have as many Italians in this squad as Paris FC , Nurnberg and Borussia Dortmund . Hell, even newly-promoted Monza has as many players in this 34-man squad as Juventus does.

During this new extended international break that lasts four games, Mancini and Italy will play four of their six UEFA Nations League group stage games. They are against Belgium (Sept. 25), Turkiye (Sept. 28), France (Oct. 2) and then a rematch with Turkiye (Oct. 5).

articles.title: Manchester United U21s 3 Brentford U21s 2: Holland brace not enough as Bees suffer narrow PL2 defeat
articles.summary: Isaac Holland found the net twice, but Brentford Under-21s were beaten 3-2 by Manchester United Under-21s in Premier League 2 at Progress With Unity Stadium...
articles.body:
Isaac Holland found the net twice, but Brentford Under-21s were beaten 3-2 by Manchester United Under-21s in Premier League 2 at Progress With Unity Stadium on Friday evening.

Holland's brace kept the Bees in the contest, but Sam Saunders' side were unable to complete a comeback as they slipped to a narrow defeat.

There were three changes to the starting XI, with Josh Oladapo-Gamu , Ben Wilson and Luca Picotto coming into the side.

The home side were controlling the possession early on and they had a chance to open the scoring through captain Jack Fletcher who managed to find space in the box and shoot from close range but Aidan Stokes did well to parry the ball away.

Despite creating little of note in the opening 19 minutes, the young Bees took the lead with a well-worked move. Caelan Avenell played a long diagonal ball towards Joseph Wheeler-Henry , who delivered a fine cross into the path of Holland, and the forward calmly slotted the ball into the net.

Following the goal, the away side were comfortable and looking the more threatening of the two teams.

However on the stroke of the half-time whistle, Amir Ibragimov struck for the home side, drilling a shot past Stokes to draw his side level in the game.

The second period saw the home side camped in Brentford's half as they continued to probe for another goal.

While clear-cut chances remained at a premium, the young Red Devils were firmly in control of proceedings.

On 63 minutes, their pressure finally paid off as defender Yuel Helafu's scuffed effort took several deflections before finding the back of the net.

Holland had the chance almost instantly to level the scoreline as he was played in on goal but the striker's shot bounced off the post.

Manchester United then extended their lead through Victor Musa, who was in the right place to finish from close range.

Second-half substitute Jai Nwosu had a golden opportunity to reduce the deficit, but his effort was saved by Cameron Byrne-Hughes.

Holland would have the final say for the Bees, completing his brace to make it 3-2, but Brentford were unable to find a late equaliser as they fell to a narrow defeat.

The defeat leaves Saunders' side with two wins and two losses from their opening four PL2 fixtures.

The Bees are next in action on Tuesday 22 September as they begin their EFL Trophy campaign away from home against Bromley.

articles.title: Texans WR Nico Collins officially ruled out for Week 2 vs. Bengals
articles.summary: The hits keep on coming for the Houston Texans and this might be the biggest in 2026 early on for the offense.
articles.body:
The hits keep on coming for the Houston Texans entering Week 2 against the Cincinnati Bengals .

On the offense? This is a big one regarding quarterback C.J. Stroud and the passing attack.

Texans Pro Bowl wide receiver Nico Collins has officially been ruled out of Sunday's showdown with a hamstring injury. Houston's top weapon did not practice the past two days and was limited on Wednesday after undergoing further testing for a hamstring strain.

Collins, who finished with a team-leading seven catches for 75 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills , has been hindered by hamstring woes since entering the league in 2021. In 2024, he missed five games with a lower-body injury after scoring a touchdown reception in the first quarter against Buffalo that required a stint on the injured reserve.

Throughout his entire career, Collins has dealt with injuries that's sidelined him for at least two games. Over the past two years, the Texans are 4-3 in that stretch in games the three-time 1,000-yard receiver has not been on the field during the regular season.

They're 0-1 in the postseason without Collins, as evidenced by the divisional round loss last January against the New England Patriots .

As a player, Collins is a monster in the passing attack. Considered a top-10 weapon in the league, he's been the Texans' most reliable vertical target when he hasn't been on the sidelines because of injuries.

And the scary part with hamstring injuries is that there's no timetable for a return, so Houston could be without Collins entering divisional play next week against the Indianapolis Colts .

Houston needs another weapon to step up this week. The Texans already lost No. 2 target Jayden Higgins to a season-ending torn ACL last month, and other weapons are still getting acclimated to the offense under second-year coordinator Nick Caley.

Knowing Collins is out, Houston should turn to newcomer Kayshon Boutte to step up as the face of the offense. In Sunday's loss, he had one catch for 21 yards.

"The good thing about the offense is we have a lot of guys that we have trust in," Caley said on Thursday. "I would say this, that we go through our reads and the ball finds the open guys. C.J. does a good job distributing the football. I think you saw that last week. We have guys that have a lot of experience with them and have played a lot of football and we'll go through it like that."

Should Boutte struggle, the Texans could turn to Jaylin Noel . The second-year product out of Iowa State was limited in his role on Sunday, he ended up catching two passes for 53 yards, averaging over 26 yards per catch.

"I thought he did great. I think he's growing; he's learning how to run routes and to be friendly to the quarterback," Stroud said of Noel's outing. "I think his speed, of course, but he's learning how to use his speed and when not to and his pace. I think he's doing a great job."

The Texans could also turn to more of a 12 (two tight ends, two receivers) or 13-personnel (one receiver, three tight ends) look with Collins sidelined and uncertainties at wide receiver. Caley praised the consistency of rookie tight end Marlin Klein after Week 1, crediting his blocking and route-running as strong reasons for growth entering Week 2.

"Marlin's coming along and done a good job. We have a deep tight end room," Caley said. "We've got a lot of guys that were at the game. He'll continue to get better and continue to build and we're very pleased with that."

articles.title: Pistons’ Locker Room May Not Respond Well to Jalen Duren’s Presence This Season
articles.summary: While the impact of the Pistons' stalemate with Jalen Duren on the Detroit locker room was already a concern, it could go nuclear. There are growing reports...
articles.body:
While the impact of the Pistons' stalemate with Jalen Duren on the Detroit locker room was already a concern, it could go nuclear. There are growing reports that Duren feels disrespected by the Pistons, suggesting he might ride out the qualifying offer into free agency to seek a fresh start.

If that happens, the upcoming season in Detroit's locker room will be an absolute mess. Unless the Pistons tell him not to suit up at all, he has to play with these guys for 2026-2027, and they may not be happy about it.

When the fight between the Pistons and Duren over his contract began months ago, the possibility of him accepting a qualifying offer seemed like a long shot at best. To be clear, it wasn't impossible, just highly improbable. Detroit had put a lot of work into becoming relevant again in the last few years, and Duren was a huge part of that. The Pistons not making this work seemed crazy.

Now, the qualifying offer route is seeming more and more likely. The negotiations have turned into what feels like silent contempt from the outside.

Duren, who is eligible for a $287 million max contract, has put a final offer of $200 million over five years on the table. Detroit responded with $190 million over five years. That's what has been reported, at least. There's still a chance that they could settle on $195 million, but the main issue may no longer be the money for Duren.

If he is, in fact, feeling disrespected by the Pistons, it would be hard to blame him. He has brought down his asking price rather dramatically and is ostensibly still being told by the front office that they don't feel he's worth that kind of money. Hopefully, no one from the organization said that to him outright, but their actions imply it. That could be enough to get Duren to head for the door.

As it stands, Duren taking the qualifying offer has gone from improbable to likely. If he feels he can get a better offer from another team in the 2027 offseason, he would need to accept that qualifying offer to maintain his unrestricted free-agent status. Essentially, Duren would be gambling on himself, knowing that other franchises, like the Sacramento Kings , might be waiting for him. That would leave Duren on the Pistons roster for the entire 2026-2027 while he waits for free agency.

That's where the locker-room response comes into play. The rest of the team getting tired of the bad press and the stress of the Duren negotiations was a real concern weeks ago . Now, the possibility of Duren playing on a qualifying offer looms over everything the Pistons are planning for the new season. It leaves them playing alongside someone they know wants out. The bad vibes will be everywhere.

Obviously, the Pistons do not need this kind of distraction from their upcoming campaign. The Eastern Conference has only gotten more competitive given the moves by other teams.

By adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown , the 76ers may have become the team to beat. Both the Hawks and the Hornets have already made net-positive changes to their rosters, which are on the rise. And the Knicks are ready and waiting to make it two championships in a row. Detroit has also made upgrades to their roster, but the Duren situation could derail their momentum.

How the Pistons Fix This Jalen Duren Situation

The front office has options to mitigate the impact of the Duren situation on their locker room. Unfortunately, none of them are good.

If Duren accepts the qualifying offer and does not come to terms with the Pistons, the Pistons could waive him. The problem is that it leaves Detroit with a bunch of dead cap space they can't do anything with. It also leaves them unable to trade him, which is complex with a player in this scenario.

An equally painful option would be benching Duren. If his presence becomes poison to the locker room, or even just a distraction, the Pistons could tell Duren not to bother suiting up and watch the games from home this season.

That would be a rather extreme choice on Detroit's part, though. It wouldn't go over well with the fans, the players, or anyone the Pistons might want to add to their roster in the future. Ultimately, they would likely end up leaving Duren in the rotation and making the best of it.

Even if Duren chooses to sign the qualifying offer, there remains the possibility that the two sides could patch up their relationship over the course of the season. Detroit could still offer him a new contract that works for both parties in the 2027 offseason. That means everyone, including the locker room, has to let go of any bad feelings that have developed over the past few months. That could be the hardest part.

articles.title: UConn football vs. Southern Miss: TV info, Keys to the game, behind the numbers
articles.summary: The Huskies enter their first road game as favorites in their first ever matchup against this Sun Belt squad.
articles.body:
UConn Huskies (1-1, FBS Independent) vs. Southern Miss Golden Eagles (1-1, 0-0 Sun Belt Conference)

Location: Carlisle-Faulkner Field at M.M. Roberts Stadium, Hattiesburg, MS

Radio: UConn Sports Network (Adam Giardino, Wayne Norman, Michael Johnson)

Fox Sports 97-9 FM (Hartford), WAVZ 1300 AM (New Haven), WGCH 1490 AM (Greenwich), WILI 1400 AM/95.3 FM (Willimantic), WICH 1310 AM/94.5 FM (Norwich-New London)

SiriusXM 269 and on the SiriusXM App 978

Odds: UConn favored -3.5, O/U: 54.5 points

This is the first time in program history that Connecticut will face off against Southern Miss. Head Coach Jason Candle has also never clashed with the Golden Eagles while at Toledo. Despite never playing each other, there are some familiar faces.

During Head Coach Blake Anderson's tenure at Arkansas State, Candle's team defeated the Red Wolves three times. The two programs also met at the 2015 GoDaddy.com Bowl, where Toledo won 63-44. UConn has also seen Anderson. In the 2022 and 2023 seasons, Anderson beat the Huskies twice while coaching at Utah State.

2: There are two former Huskies on the Golden Eagles' roster. Defensive back Kobi Albert is a redshirt junior and joined UConn in 2025, as did defensive back Michael Robinson III.

Michael Robinson III also transferred to Southern Miss after playing in two games during UConn's 2025 stretch, but didn't post any stats. In two matches with the Golden Eagles, the 6-foot, 190-pound defensive back has notched nine tackles (five solo, four assisted) and forced a fumble against Auburn.

3: Since the 2022 season, Connecticut has faced three different Sun Belt opponents: Marshall in the 2022 Myrtle Beach Bowl, a 28-14 loss; Georgia State on the road, falling 35-14 in 2023; and a James Madison team that destroyed them, 44-6). The Huskies own a 1-3 overall record against Sun Belt opponents since 2022. They'll play three Sun Belt opponents this year: USM, James Madison, and Old Dominion.

4: The former Husky Albert has recorded four turnovers thus far, including three interceptions and a fumble recovery against Auburn.

5: The Golden Eagles were picked to finish 5th out of seven in their division in the Sun Belt preseason poll.

613: The Southern Miss defense allowed 613 total offensive yards (270 passing, 343 rushing) against Auburn.

41: Last time Jason Candle was in the state of Mississippi, his Toledo Rockets defeated the SEC's Mississippi State, 41-17.

UConn's offense came up flat against Maryland. That was a Big Ten opponent and a team that's had a top-50 defense in each of the last three years.

This week, the Huskies will look to establish the run early and prove that they can score in a more even matchup against the Golden Eagles. Quarterback Kalieb Osborne didn't have the strongest numbers last week, in his third career start. But he has lots of promise and the poise to lead the bounce-back UConn needs. Through two weeks, he's displayed a fun combination of mobility, arm strength, and decision-making.

"All around, [we] have to get the energy going a little bit. It starts off at the first play; you have to attack them," wide receiver Shamar Porter said. "Once you get going as an offense, you have to attack them [and] come ready every play. 6-second plays and you have to go on to the next."

On third down, the Huskies only moved the chains 3 of 11 times, facing an average third-down to-go of 8.3 yards last week. The run game was a non-factor. Kenji Christian (17 yards) and Cyncir Bowers (12 yards) combined for 29 rushing yards on the day. These guys have to get going and make sure the Husky defense has enough rest.

"We just have to execute, finish our runs, trust our keys and do what we have to do," Bowers said.

UConn forced the Terrapins' gunslinger, Malik Washington , out of the pocket several times, but he stayed mostly clean and they completed a lot of passes in tight windows — a credit to Washington and his receivers.

"Those kids on the defensive front played their tail off," Candle said, noting that he's confident in the secondary going forward.

The Huskies finished with one sack, one QB hurry, and haven't forced a turnover through two games this season. For a defense that billed itself as aggressive, this needs to change. The Golden Eagles turned the ball over twice in their 43-8 loss to Auburn last week.

The Husky defense may give us some scoring drives, but they the size and depth to make enough stops on Saturday. They face a Golden Eagles offense that is totally rebuilt after a coaching change this offseason, like UConn, but their key players are experienced. Quarterback Ethan Hampton spent four years at Northern Illinois; they have two reliable backs in Steven Robinson and Jamarice Wilder, and a top receiver in Mario Sanders II who has been productive.

UConn was tested against Maryland, but the talent advantage played out how we expected. In a game where the talent should be at least even, if not skewing in the Huskies' favor a little, this needs to show up defensively.

Javon Brown broke out in a big way in Week 1 and earned high praise from Candle for his development and work ethic. He followed that up with zero catches against Maryland but is a threat to re-establish himself this week. JD Willoughby has also shown his big-play ability after the 37-yard touchdown against the Terps. He also had a long touchdown reversed by penalty in the opener against Lafayette.

In his third year as a Husky, Shamar Porter posted a career-high 62 receiving yards against Maryland last week, adding a touchdown. Candle said the senior should continue to be a playmaker as he gets more comfortable with the new offensive scheme.

articles.title: Alabama football news: AK Dear's injury status for Florida State game gets update
articles.summary: The No. 10 Alabama Crimson Tide is scheduled to face off against the Florida State Seminoles on Saturday in a highly anticipated Week 3 matchup. However, run...
articles.body:
The No. 10 Alabama Crimson Tide is scheduled to face off against the Florida State Seminoles on Saturday in a highly anticipated Week 3 matchup. However, running back AK Dear is currently dealing with an injury . The latest injury update reveals Dear's official status for the contest on Friday.

Reports indicate that the redshirt freshman is deemed questionable for the game against the Seminoles, according to Pete Nakos of On3 Sports. Dear has yet to make his 2026-27 season debut, as he is still recovering from an ankle injury he suffered during the preseason.

"Alabama running back AK Dear is questionable for Saturday's rematch with Florida State, sources tell On3," Nakos said. "He continues to recover from a preseason ankle injury."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Crimson Tide will rely on Daniel Hill in the backfield in Week 3. True freshman Trae'shawn Brown is listed as the immediate backup for now. However, whenever AK Dear does finally return from the ankle injury, he should be given a chance to work as the backup option in Alabama.

Dear appeared in five games last season as a true freshman. He only had 19 attempts, but flashed major potential with limited opportunities. He finished last season with 140 yards and three touchdowns, giving him an impressive average of 7.4 yards per attempt.

While the Mississippi native continues to progress through his injury, Alabama will have a chance to earn its third win on the season. The Crimson Tide has looked solid so far this year, with blow out wins over the East Carolina Pirates and Kentucky Wildcats.
